transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I honestly just can't see my studio or my life getting back on track anymore. It doesn't seem to matter how hard I work, or, you know, what kind of payment plan they put in front of me. I just don't see a way out of this.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much every day. Most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me, and it just stays there. Even when I'm out in the shop, surrounded by the wood I used to love working with, everything just feels flat now. Honestly, I have to fight with myself not to just stand there staring at nothing.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, it's been going on since I took on the mortgage for the studio... so that was a little over two years ago. I'd say about two years and two months now, if I had to put a number on it.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt the opposite—unusually energized, hyper, or on top of the world, needing very little sleep?
No, I haven't. I mean... I've never felt anything like that. I've never been hyper or felt on top of the world, and I definitely always need my sleep. So, no, nothing like what you're describing.
During these past two years, has there ever been a period of two months or more where you felt like your usual self?

No, definitely not. I mean... maybe I've had a day or two where things felt a little lighter, but never weeks or months at a time. It's just been this same heavy feeling straight through the whole two years. There hasn't been any real break from it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over this time?
No, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the same. I mean, I still eat my regular meals and all that. So no, I haven't noticed any big changes with my appetite or my weight.
How has your sleep been over these past two years?

My sleep? It's been pretty normal, honestly. I usually get about seven or eight hours a night. I mean, sometimes I'm tired from work—being on my feet all day takes it out of you—but I don't have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. So, yeah, no real issues there.
Have you been feeling a persistent lack of energy or excessive fatigue?

Yeah, definitely. Even after getting a full night in bed, I still feel completely wiped out. By midmorning, my arms feel like I've been hauling lumber all day. It's... it's just really hard to push through the normal stuff. Just measuring, cutting, or even returning phone calls takes everything out of me. I just have zero energy.
How has your self-esteem or the way you feel about yourself been during this time?

Not great, honestly. I've been pretty down on myself. It's like... well, at work, if a joint doesn't line up perfect, or if I end up missing a bid deadline, I don't just think that I made a simple mistake. I take it really hard. I start thinking I'm just a lousy carpenter. It gets in my head, and I start telling myself that maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place. So yeah, I guess I haven't been feeling too good about myself.
